steps: Proposer sends prepare with a new ballot number.
Quorum promises not to accept older ballots and reports prior accepted values.
Proposer must carry the highest prior value, then requests acceptance.
Quorum acceptance chooses the value and learners apply it.

lesson.scenario: A single-decree Paxos round chooses one configuration value even when a newer proposer encounters an earlier partial acceptance.

steps.title: Persist an earlier partial acceptance
steps.narration: Before ballot 7 begins, A1 has durably accepted value blue at ballot 6, while A2 and A3 have no accepted value; no quorum chose ballot 6 yet.

learner.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: A later proposer must preserve the possible chosen value.
steps.invariant: Acceptors persist promises and accepted pairs before replying, a proposer uses a majority and adopts the value with the highest accepted ballot it hears, and any learned choice requires matching acceptances from a quorum.

steps.title: Prepare a higher ballot
steps.narration: A1 and A2 form a majority and durably promise not to accept ballots below 7; A1 returns its accepted pair (6,blue).

learner.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: Ballot 7 owns a quorum of promises and learns prior acceptance.
steps.invariant: Acceptors persist promises and accepted pairs before replying, a proposer uses a majority and adopts the value with the highest accepted ballot it hears, and any learned choice requires matching acceptances from a quorum.

steps.title: Adopt the highest accepted value
steps.narration: Although P7 preferred green, Phase 1 requires it to propose blue, the value with the highest accepted ballot in its promise quorum.
action: Return accepted value blue from ballot 6

learner.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: Intersecting quorums cannot be led toward conflicting values.
steps.invariant: Acceptors persist promises and accepted pairs before replying, a proposer uses a majority and adopts the value with the highest accepted ballot it hears, and any learned choice requires matching acceptances from a quorum.

steps.title: Accept on a majority
steps.narration: A1 and A2 accept and persist (7,blue) because ballot 7 meets their promises; a delayed AcceptRequest(6,green) is rejected.
steps.outcome: Value blue is chosen by majority {A1,A2}.
steps.invariant: Acceptors persist promises and accepted pairs before replying, a proposer uses a majority and adopts the value with the highest accepted ballot it hears, and any learned choice requires matching acceptances from a quorum.

steps.title: Learn the immutable choice
steps.narration: The learner writes slot 41=blue with quorum proof A1,A2; future proposers intersect this quorum and must carry blue forward.
action: Record blue after two matching acceptances
steps.outcome: The slot exposes one safe chosen configuration despite failures and retries.

production.scenario: Google Ads campaign budget controls must agree on one rollout value across zones before millions of bids use it.
components: global campaign managers changing budget caps and pacing controls
service boundary that validates config writes and exposes them to the control plane
control-plane service that uses Paxos rounds to choose one budget config value per rollout slot
durable authority in Spanner for chosen config values and rollout epochs
uses only chosen budget values when pacing live auction decisions
control-plane service that drains replicas, repairs failed zones, and orchestrates proposer changes
observability path for quorum health, proposal retries, and rollout latency
flows: Operators submit a new campaign pacing configuration that must be globally agreed before use.
The config boundary asks Paxos to choose a single value for the next rollout slot.
The chosen config and epoch are committed to the authoritative decision ledger.
The bid-serving fleet loads only the config values marked chosen in the durable ledger.
Quorum operations drains unhealthy members and changes proposer routing under supervision.
The decision ledger identifies stuck or superseded proposals for targeted remediation.
Dashboards show retry storms, quorum loss risk, and decision latency during peak traffic.
